rules.ask: This parameter's name ($NAME) misdescribes how the function's body uses it.
rules.note: Only the parameter in `matched` is judged; the function's other parameters are separate subjects and the surrounding code is context. Read every use of that parameter in the body: which argument position it fills and what that position means (the first argument of slice is a start index, the argument of setTimeout is milliseconds), what it is compared with or concatenated to and on which side, what it is multiplied or divided by, which fields are read from it, and whether it is called. The type annotation is not the evidence -- it type-checks either way -- the name is the claim and what the body does with the value is the evidence. A body that only passes the parameter on, stores it, or returns it shows nothing against the name.
rules.subject: enclosing
